title: Dewey Selmon: OU Nose Guard Turned Builder and Hall of Famer
question: What did Dewey Selmon do after playing football at Oklahoma?
answer: Dewey Selmon, who played at Oklahoma from 1972 to 1975, spent seven seasons in the NFL and then opened his own construction business. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2024.
summary: Dewey Selmon anchored OU's 1974 and 1975 title teams, played seven NFL seasons, started a construction business and entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2024.
body: Dewey Selmon played at Oklahoma from 1972 to 1975 under Barry Switzer. He was a nose guard who also lined up at defensive tackle, and he started on the Sooner defensive line from 1973 through 1975. Older brother Lucious was already a starter when he arrived, and in his first two seasons he shared the field with both Lucious and Lee Roy.

Those teams won constantly. Oklahoma claimed back-to-back national championships in 1974 and 1975, and the Sooners went 32-1-1 in his years as a starter. Selmon finished with 325 tackles and 25 tackles for loss, and he was a first-team All-American in 1974 and a consensus All-American in 1975. He was also a two-time Academic All-American.
The pros came next. Tampa Bay chose him in the second round of the 1976 NFL Draft, and he played seven NFL seasons, six of them with the Buccaneers, finishing with the San Diego Chargers.

Back home, he went into business for himself and opened a construction company. According to the National Football Foundation, he has also devoted much of his life to young people in need, including several trips to West Africa to help build a school for an orphanage. His children started the Shine Foundation, a nonprofit that serves people in need.
The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in the class of 2024, joining his brother Lee Roy, who was inducted in 1988.
